investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only. All retained evidence acquired via plain curl (raw HTTP, no WebFetch/AI-markdown conversion, real descriptive User-Agent) against: the venue's own homepage, the given candidate 'Agenda de Fados' page (verified as the correct, live events page — not corrected, it was already right), the site's wp-json REST route listing, and its RSS feed. Inspected the retained agenda-page HTML for JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent data (none found — only standard Yoast WebPage/Organization schema), ICS export links (none found), known calendar-plugin fingerprints (none found — bespoke Elementor + Premium-Addons-for-Elementor page, not The Events Calendar/EventOn/Squarespace), and a plain server-rendered day-by-day performer list (found: 31 sequential day-blocks, one per day of August 2026, each pairing a DD/MM heading + Portuguese weekday name + a performer-names paragraph). A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script re-parsed the retained HTML/JSON/XML files to mechanically re-derive every claim below, including a real Gregorian-calendar cross-check (year taken from the page's own 'AGOSTO 2026' heading, never from today's real-world date) confirming all 31 day-blocks' self-stated weekday names are internally consistent. Level 1 was SUFFICIENT; no escalation to Level 2/3/4 was attempted.

probe_history.reason: Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) of https://famadalfama.pt (homepage), https://famadalfama.pt/agenda-de-fados-em-lisboa/ (the given candidate events page), https://famadalfama.pt/wp-json/ (REST route listing), and https://famadalfama.pt/feed/ (RSS) all returned 200 OK. The agenda page's raw, unrendered HTML already contained the ENTIRE month of August 2026 as 31 sequential, fully server-rendered day-blocks (date + weekday + performer names) with no JS execution needed to reveal them — confirmed by grepping the retained static file directly for all 31 'DD/MM' headings. The homepage's own Yoast JSON-LD Organization node and footer address independently confirmed venue identity. The wp-json route listing (383 routes) contained no agenda/event/fado/calendar-shaped custom REST route, and the RSS feed contained zero <item> entries, ruling out PUBLIC_JSON_API and RSS as usable data paths. This already answers identity, platform classification, data-path discovery, and field assessment for a genuine nightly-recurring-performer calendar without needing to inspect JS bundles or open a browser, so escalation to Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) or beyond was not attempted.

venue_reference: Fama D'Alfama — fado house / restaurant, Rua do Terreiro do Trigo 80, Alfama, Lisboa, Portugal

identity.notes: Independently re-confirmed by this investigation's own retained evidence, not assumed from the prior loose note. The homepage's own Yoast schema-graph JSON-LD names an Organization node {"name": "Fama D'Alfama Restaurante", "url": "https://famadalfama.pt/"} with sameAs links to the venue's own Facebook (facebook.com/restaurantefamadalfama), Instagram (instagram.com/famadalfama), and TripAdvisor listing. The homepage footer independently states the street address 'Rua do Terreiro do Trigo 80' (Alfama, Lisboa — the neighbourhood and city are also explicitly stated in the homepage <title> 'Fama D'Alfama - Gastronomia e Fado Autêntico em Lisboa' and meta description). The agenda page shares the same canonical domain, the same Organization JSON-LD (via the site-wide Yoast graph), and its own <title> 'Agenda de Fados - Fama D'Alfama'. No postal code or a full multi-line postal address was found in the retained evidence — only the street address and city name are established this way, which is sufficient for PROVEN identity but noted honestly as a minor gap, not smoothed over.

site_classification.platform: WordPress (theme built on Elementor + Elementor Pro, with 'Premium Addons for Elementor' (its 'Display Conditions' feature, visible as pa-display-conditions-yes markers) and ElementsKit Lite) — a bespoke, hand-authored monthly calendar built as 31 sequential Elementor page sections directly inside one static page, not a recognisable off-the-shelf events/calendar plugin (not The Events Calendar, EventOn, or Squarespace). No JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent data is emitted anywhere (only the standard Yoast SEO WebPage/Organization/BreadcrumbList graph). No ICS export link was found. The site's wp-json REST route listing (383 routes) contains no agenda/event/fado/calendar-shaped custom route, and its RSS feed carries zero items — both checked and ruled out, not merely unchecked. The entire month's day-by-day performer schedule is present verbatim in the plain server-rendered HTML of the one agenda page; no client-side rendering or hidden data path was needed to read it.

data_paths.kind: WP_JSON_REST_ROOT (checked — no agenda/event-shaped custom route exists)
RSS_FEED (checked — zero <item> entries, no blog-post-based events)

title.notes: Each of the 31 day-blocks carries its own non-empty performer-names paragraph — the closest thing this source has to an event 'title' (there is no separate abstract show name; the performers ARE the listing, e.g. '01/08': 'Miguel Dias & Matilde Cid / Tomás Pauseiro – Guitarra Portuguesa / Diogo de Castro – Viola de Fado'). Verified mechanically for all 31/31 day-blocks (none empty) in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt. Left null here (a general capability finding across the full retained month, not one single event) — see evidence/offline-proof-output.txt for the actual per-day values, including the first 3 and last 3 as a representative sample.

start_date.notes: The agenda page states the month/year exactly once ('AGOSTO 2026' heading) and each of the 31 day-blocks states its own day-of-month ('01/08' .. '31/08') plus its own Portuguese weekday name (e.g. 'Sábado', 'Domingo'). This gives a full calendar date per entry without inventing anything: the year and month come directly from the page's own explicit heading text, not from today's real-world date or any external assumption. This was cross-checked mechanically and NOT merely trusted: evidence/offline-proof.mjs recomputes, using pure Gregorian calendar arithmetic for the year 2026 (again, taken from the source's own stated heading — never from 'today'), the real weekday for every one of the 31 dates and confirms all 31/31 match the source's own stated weekday name exactly. This is a floating local date — no explicit UTC offset or IANA timezone is stated anywhere in the retained HTML; Europe/Lisbon is the obvious real-world timezone but this was never promoted to a fabricated UTC instant.

time.notes: The retained page states, once, in a shared (site-wide footer) text block: 'Abrimos às 19h00' (opens 19:00) / 'Fado a partir das 20h30' (fado from 20:30). This is a genuine, unambiguous, explicit statement of the nightly fado start time — but it is a PAGE-LEVEL / VENUE-LEVEL constant, not a value re-stated inside each of the 31 day-blocks individually (mechanically confirmed: none of the 31 day-block matches in evidence/offline-proof.mjs contain their own distinct time text). No exception to this shared time was observed anywhere in the retained sample. A collector should treat 20h30 as the applicable start time for every night on this page unless a future re-fetch shows the source stating a per-night exception, which this investigation did not observe. Floating local time, same timezone caveat as start_date.

end.notes: No end time or duration is stated anywhere in the retained homepage or agenda-page HTML, for the page as a whole or for any individual day-block.

venue_location.notes: Every night's performance is at the venue's own single physical address — the source does not vary location per day-block (unlike, e.g., an outdoor-vs-indoor concert hall). The homepage footer (site-wide, present on the agenda page too via the same header/footer template) states the street address 'Rua do Terreiro do Trigo 80'; the city 'Lisboa' is explicitly stated in the homepage's own <title> and meta description. No postal code or geocoordinates were found in retained evidence, so precision beyond street + city is not proven — recorded honestly rather than guessed.

source_record_id.notes: The source exposes NO id token of any kind for an individual night's performance — no data-attribute id, no per-day permalink/slug, no JSON-LD @id (there is no JSON-LD Event data at all on this source). Confirmed mechanically: evidence/offline-proof.mjs verifies zero of the 31 day-blocks contain their own <a href>, and the wp-json route listing has no agenda/event-shaped REST route that might expose one either. Per the stable-identifier rule, this must stay NOT_PRESENT rather than inventing a random hash. DOCUMENTED ALTERNATIVE IDENTITY STRATEGY (satisfying the READY_FOR_ACTIVATION gate's 'explicit alternative identity strategy' clause): a future collector should synthesize a composite key of (venue_reference + the calendar date derived from the page's own 'AGOSTO 2026' heading + each day-block's own 'DD/MM' heading, e.g. 'fama-dalfama-lisbon-01:2026-08-17'). This is safe because the source's own structure guarantees at most one day-block per calendar date — mechanically confirmed in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt (31 day-blocks, strictly ascending 1..31, no duplicate dates) — so (venue, date) is a genuine 1:1 key for this source's granularity, even though the source itself never states an opaque id.

event_url.notes: The source provides no per-night permalink — all 31 day-blocks share exactly one URL, the agenda page itself (https://famadalfama.pt/agenda-de-fados-em-lisboa/). Mechanically confirmed: evidence/offline-proof.mjs verifies zero of the 31 day-blocks contain their own <a href> anchor. A collector can honestly report this single shared page URL as 'where this fact was read', but it must never be treated as, or synthesized into, a distinct per-occurrence URL — hence PARTIAL rather than PROVEN (a URL genuinely exists and is reliably extractable, but it is not unique per record).

price.notes: No price, admission fee, ticket cost, or currency symbol ('€') was found anywhere in the retained homepage or agenda-page HTML (this is a restaurant with a nightly show, not a ticketed venue with a stated admission price on this page — a menu/reservation price may exist elsewhere on the site but was not part of this investigation's bounded retained sample).

blockers.description: No source-documented per-night identifier exists (see field_assessment.source_record_id.notes). A collector must synthesize a composite (venue_reference + calendar date) key rather than relying on any id from the source itself.

The nightly fado start time (20h30) is stated once as a page-level/venue-level constant, not repeated per day-block. A genuine per-night exception (e.g. a special/holiday schedule) would not be caught by a collector that hard-codes this constant unless the source's own markup changes to state it — this investigation observed no such exception in its retained sample, but did not test for one either.

This investigation observed only a single snapshot of the agenda page, covering exactly the calendar month 'AGOSTO 2026'. The retained homepage's article:modified_time (2026-08-03T10:48:34Z, itself retained evidence) suggests the page is edited in place at least once during a given month, which is suggestive but not empirical proof that the same URL reliably rolls over to the next month (September 2026) with the same structure. A collector should re-observe this URL after the month boundary before relying on continuity, rather than assuming it from this one snapshot.
